- [Create a Kubernetes cluster](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/post-lke-cluster.md): Creates a Kubernetes cluster. The Kubernetes cluster will be created asynchronously. You can use the events system to determine when the Kubernetes cluster is ready to use. Please note that it often takes 2-5 minutes before the [Kubernetes API endpoints](ref:get-lke-cluster-api-endpoints) and the [Kubeconfig file](ref:get-lke-cluster-kubeconfig) for the new cluster are ready.   **Permissions and scopes**  To call this operation, you need the following:  - **Identity and access permissions**. Your user needs these roles assigned. [Learn more](https://techdocs.akamai.com/cloud-computing/docs/identity-access-cm-available-roles).   - Roles: `account_lkecluster_creator` - **OAuth scopes**. Your user needs these scopes assigned. [Learn more](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-started#oauth).    - Scopes: `lke:read_write`   **CLI**  ```shell linode-cli lke cluster-create \   --label cluster12345 \   --region us-central \   --k8s_version 1.33 \   --apl_enabled false \   --control_plane.high_availability true \   --node_pools.type g6-standard-4 --node_pools.count 6 \   --node_pools.type g6-standard-8 --node_pools.count 3 \   --node_pools.autoscaler.enabled true \   --node_pools.autoscaler.max 12 \   --node_pools.autoscaler.min 3 \   --tags ecomm ```  [Learn more](https://techdocs.akamai.com/cloud-computing/docs/getting-started-with-the-linode-cli)

- [Update a Kubernetes cluster](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/put-lke-cluster.md): Updates a Kubernetes cluster.   **Permissions and scopes**  To call this operation, you need the following:  - **Identity and access permissions**. Your user needs these scopes assigned. - [Delete a Kubernetes cluster](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/delete-lke-cluster.md): Deletes a cluster from your account.  > 🚧 > > Deleting a cluster is a destructive action and can't be undone.  When a cluster is deleted, all supporting Kubernetes services are removed from your account along with all Linodes in your cluster's node pools. You must have `read_write` permission to the cluster to initiate deletion.  Some additional services associated with your cluster remain active on your account. These services include NodeBalancers and Block Storage volumes. To avoid further charges, delete these services manually through Cloud Manager, the Linode CLI, or the Linode API.  Account administrators can configure a resource lock with the [Create a resource lock](ref:post-resource-lock) operation to prevent a cluster from being deleted. They can also remove the lock with the [Delete a resource lock](ref:delete-resource-lock) operation.   **Permissions and scopes**  To call this operation, you need the following:  - **Identity and access permissions**. Your user needs these roles assigned. [Learn more](https://techdocs.akamai.com/cloud-computing/docs/identity-access-cm-available-roles).   - Roles: `lkecluster_admin` - **OAuth scopes**. Your user needs these scopes assigned. [Learn more](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-started#oauth).    - Scopes: `lke:read_write`   **CLI**  ```shell linode-cli lke cluster-delete 12345 ```  [Learn more](https://techdocs.akamai.com/cloud-computing/docs/getting-started-with-the-linode-cli)
- [Recycle cluster nodes](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/post-lke-cluster-recycle.md): Recycles all nodes in all pools of a designated Kubernetes Cluster. All Linodes within the Cluster will be deleted and replaced with new Linodes on a rolling basis, which may take several minutes. Replacement Nodes are installed with the latest available patch version for the Cluster's current Kubernetes minor release.  __Any local storage on deleted Linodes (such as `hostPath` and `emptyDir` volumes, or `local` PersistentVolumes) will be erased.__   **Permissions and scopes**  To call this operation, you need the following:  - **OAuth scopes**. Your user needs these scopes assigned. [Learn more](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-started#oauth).    - Scopes: `lke:read_write`   **CLI**  ```shell linode-cli lke cluster-nodes-recycle 12345 ```  [Learn more](https://techdocs.akamai.com/cloud-computing/docs/getting-started-with-the-linode-cli)
- [Regenerate a Kubernetes cluster](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/post-lke-cluster-regenerate.md): Regenerate the Kubeconfig file and/or the service account token for a Cluster.  This is a helper operation that allows performing both the [Delete a Kubeconfig](ref:delete-lke-cluster-kubeconfig) and the [Delete a service token](ref:delete-lke-service-token) operations with a single request.  When using this operation, at least one of `kubeconfig` or `servicetoken` is required.  > 📘 > > When regenerating a service account token, the cluster's control plane components and Linode CSI drivers are also restarted and configured with the new token. High availability clusters shouldn't experience any disruption, while standard clusters may experience brief control plane downtime while components are restarted.   **Permissions and scopes**  To call this operation, you need the following:  - **Identity and access permissions**. Your user needs these roles assigned. [Learn more](https://techdocs.akamai.com/cloud-computing/docs/identity-access-cm-available-roles).   - Roles: `lkecluster_admin` - **OAuth scopes**. Your user needs these scopes assigned. [Learn more](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-started#oauth).    - Scopes: `lke:read_write`   **CLI**  ```shell linode-cli lke regenerate 12345 \     --kubeconfig true \     --servicetoken true ```  [Learn more](https://techdocs.akamai.com/cloud-computing/docs/getting-started-with-the-linode-cli)

- [Delete the control plane access control list](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/delete-lke-cluster-acl.md): Disables control plane access controls and deletes all rules. - [Get a Kubernetes cluster dashboard URL](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-lke-cluster-dashboard.md): __Deprecated__ This operation has been deprecated. This change occurred in May 2026. The Kubernetes Dashboard is no longer available for existing LKE clusters and can't deploy to new clusters.   **Permissions and scopes**  To call this operation, you need the following:  - **Identity and access permissions**. - [Create a node pool](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/post-lke-cluster-pools.md): Creates a new node pool for the designated Kubernetes cluster.   **Permissions and scopes**  To call this operation, you need the following:  - **Identity and access permissions**. - [Update a node pool](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/put-lke-node-pool.md): Updates a node pool's count, labels, taints, and autoscaler configuration.  Linodes are created or deleted to match changes to the node pool's count.  Specifying labels or taints on update overwrites any previous values, and updates existing nodes with the new values without a recycle.  __Any local storage on deleted Linodes (such as `hostPath` and `emptyDir` volumes, or `local` PersistentVolumes) will be erased.__   **Permissions and scopes**  To call this operation, you need the following:  - **Identity and access permissions**. Your user needs these roles assigned. [Learn more](https://techdocs.akamai.com/cloud-computing/docs/identity-access-cm-available-roles).   - Roles: `lkecluster_admin` - **OAuth scopes**. Your user needs these scopes assigned. [Learn more](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-started#oauth).    - Scopes: `lke:read_write`   **CLI**  ```shell linode-cli lke pool-update 12345 456 \   --count 6 \   --autoscaler.enabled true \   --autoscaler.max 12 \   --autoscaler.min 3 \   --labels '{ "example.com/my-app":"team1", "env":"staging" }' \   --taints.effect "NoSchedule" \   --taints.key "example.com/my-app" \   --taints.value "teamA" ```  [Learn more](https://techdocs.akamai.com/cloud-computing/docs/getting-started-with-the-linode-cli)
- [Delete a node pool](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/delete-lke-node-pool.md): Delete a specific node pool from a Kubernetes cluster.  __Deleting a node pool is a destructive action and can't be undone.__  Deleting a node pool deletes all Linodes within that pool.  Account administrators can configure a resource lock with the [Create a resource lock](ref:post-resource-lock) operation to prevent a node pool from being deleted. They can also remove the lock with the [Delete a resource lock](ref:delete-resource-lock) operation.   **Permissions and scopes**  To call this operation, you need the following:  - **Identity and access permissions**. Your user needs these scopes assigned. [Learn more](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/get-started#oauth).    - Scopes: `lke:read_write`   **CLI**  ```shell linode-cli lke pool-delete 12345 456 ```  [Learn more](https://techdocs.akamai.com/cloud-computing/docs/getting-started-with-the-linode-cli)

- [Delete a service token](https://techdocs.akamai.com/linode-api/reference/delete-lke-service-token.md): Delete and regenerate the service account token for a Cluster.  > 📘 > > When you regenerate a service account token, the cluster's control plane components and Linode CSI drivers are also restarted and configured with the new token. blocks.text: Create a Kubernetes cluster: Creates a Kubernetes cluster. The Kubernetes cluster will be created asynchronously. You can use the events system to determine when the Kubernetes cluster is ready to use. Please note that it often takes 2-5 minutes before the Kubernetes API endpoints and the Kubeconfig file for the new cluster are ready.   Permissions and scopes  To call this operation, you need the following:  - Identity and access permissions. Your user needs these roles assigned. Learn more.   - Roles: account_lkecluster_creator - OAuth scopes. Your user needs these scopes assigned. Learn more.    - Scopes: lke:read_write   CLI  shell linode-cli lke cluster-create \   --label cluster12345 \   --region us-central \   --k8s_version 1.33 \   --apl_enabled false \   --control_plane.high_availability true \   --node_pools.type g6-standard-4 --node_pools.count 6 \   --node_pools.type g6-standard-8 --node_pools.count 3 \   --node_pools.autoscaler.enabled true \   --node_pools.autoscaler.max 12 \   --node_pools.autoscaler.min 3 \   --tags ecomm   Learn moreList Kubernetes clusters: Lists current Kubernetes clusters available on your account.   Permissions and scopes  To call this operation, you need the following:  - Identity and access permissions. Your user needs these roles assigned. Learn more.   - Roles: lkecluster_viewer - OAuth scopes. Your user needs these scopes assigned. Learn more.    - Scopes: lke:read_only   CLI  shell linode-cli lke clusters-list   Learn moreGet a Kubernetes cluster: Get a specific Cluster by ID.   Permissions and scopes  To call this operation, you need the following:  - Identity and access permissions. Your user needs these roles assigned. Learn more.   - Roles: lkecluster_viewer - OAuth scopes. Your user needs these scopes assigned. Learn more.    - Scopes: lke:read_only   CLI  shell linode-cli lke cluster-view 12345   Learn moreUpdate a Kubernetes cluster: Updates a Kubernetes cluster.   Permissions and scopes  To call this operation, you need the following:  - Identity and access permissions. Your user needs these roles assigned. Learn more.   - Roles: lkecluster_admin - OAuth scopes. Your user needs these scopes assigned. Learn more.    - Scopes: lke:read_write   CLI  shell linode-cli lke cluster-update 12345 \   --label lkecluster54321 \   --control_plane.high_availability true \   --k8s_version 1.33 \   --tags ecomm \   --tags blog \   --tags prod \   --tags monitoring   Learn moreDelete a Kubernetes cluster: Deletes a cluster from your account.  > 🚧 > > Deleting a cluster is a destructive action and can't be undone.  When a cluster is deleted, all supporting Kubernetes services are removed from your account along with all Linodes in your cluster's node pools. You must have read_write permission to the cluster to initiate deletion.  Some additional services associated with your cluster remain active on your account. These services include NodeBalancers and Block Storage volumes. To avoid further charges, delete these services manually through Cloud Manager, the Linode CLI, or the Linode API.  Account administrators can configure a resource lock with the Create a resource lock operation to prevent a cluster from being deleted. They can also remove the lock with the Delete a resource lock operation.   Permissions and scopes  To call this operation, you need the following:  - Identity and access permissions. Your user needs these roles assigned. Learn more.   - Roles: lkecluster_admin - OAuth scopes. Your user needs these scopes assigned. Learn more.    - Scopes: lke:read_write   CLI  shell linode-cli lke cluster-delete 12345   Learn moreRecycle cluster nodes: Recycles all nodes in all pools of a designated Kubernetes Cluster. All Linodes within the Cluster will be deleted and replaced with new Linodes on a rolling basis, which may take several minutes. Replacement Nodes are installed with the latest available patch version for the Cluster's current Kubernetes minor release.  Any local storage on deleted Linodes (such as hostPath and emptyDir volumes, or local PersistentVolumes) will be erased.   Permissions and scopes  To call this operation, you need the following:  - OAuth scopes. Your user needs these scopes assigned. Learn more.    - Scopes: lke:read_write   CLI  shell linode-cli lke cluster-nodes-recycle 12345   Learn moreRegenerate a Kubernetes cluster: Regenerate the Kubeconfig file and/or the service account token for a Cluster.  This is a helper operation that allows performing both the Delete a Kubeconfig and the Delete a service token operations with a single request.  When using this operation, at least one of kubeconfig or servicetoken is required.  > 📘 > > When regenerating a service account token, the cluster's control plane components and Linode CSI drivers are also restarted and configured with the new token. High availability clusters shouldn't experience any disruption, while standard clusters may experience brief control plane downtime while components are restarted.   Permissions and scopes  To call this operation, you need the following:  - Identity and access permissions. Your user needs these roles assigned. Learn more.   - Roles: lkecluster_admin - OAuth scopes. Your user needs these scopes assigned. Learn more.    - Scopes: lke:read_write   CLI  shell linode-cli lke regenerate 12345 \     --kubeconfig true \     --servicetoken true   Learn moreGet the control plane access control list: Get a specific cluster's control plane access control List.   Permissions and scopes  To call this operation, you need the following:  - Identity and access permissions. Your user needs these roles assigned. Learn more.   - Roles: lkecluster_viewer - OAuth scopes. Your user needs these scopes assigned. Learn more.    - Scopes: lke:read_only   CLI  shell linode-cli lke cluster-acl-view 12345   Learn moreUpdate the control plane access control list: Updates a specific cluster's control plane access control list.   Permissions and scopes  To call this operation, you need the following:  - Identity and access permissions. Your user needs these roles assigned. Learn more.   - Roles: lkecluster_admin - OAuth scopes. Your user needs these scopes assigned. Learn more.    - Scopes: lke:read_write   CLI  shell linode-cli lke cluster-acl-update 12345 \       --acl.enabled true \       --acl.addresses.ipv4 "203.0.113.1" \       --acl.addresses.ipv6 "2001:db8:1234:abcd::/64"   Learn moreDelete the control plane access control list: Disables control plane access controls and deletes all rules. It has the same effect as calling PUT with an ACL JSON map value of {"enabled": false}.   Permissions and scopes  To call this operation, you need the following:  - Identity and access permissions. Your user needs these roles assigned. Learn more.   - Roles: lkecluster_admin - OAuth scopes. Your user needs these scopes assigned. Learn more.    - Scopes: lke:read_write   CLI  shell linode-cli lke cluster-acl-delete 12345   Learn moreGet a Kubernetes cluster dashboard URL: Deprecated This operation has been deprecated. It previously returned the URL for the Kubernetes Dashboard installed on your cluster, which enabled performance of administrative tasks through a web interface. See Using the Kubernetes Dashboard on LKE.  > ❗️ LKE’s Kubernetes Dashboard has been decommissioned > > Following the upstream archival of the Kubernetes Dashboard project, Akamai Cloud decommissioned the LKE-hosted Kubernetes Dashboard. This change occurred in May 2026. The Kubernetes Dashboard is no longer available for existing LKE clusters and can't deploy to new clusters.   Permissions and scopes  To call this operation, you need the following:  - Identity and access permissions. Your user needs these roles assigned. Learn more.   - Roles: lkecluster_viewer - OAuth scopes. Your user needs these scopes assigned. Learn more.    - Scopes: lke:read_write   CLI  shell linode-cli lke kubeconfig-view 12345   Learn moreDelete a Kubeconfig: Delete and regenerate the Kubeconfig file for a Cluster. Permissions and scopes  To call this operation, you need the following:  - Identity and access permissions. Your user needs these roles assigned. Specifying labels or taints on update overwrites any previous values, and updates existing nodes with the new values without a recycle.
